title: Composition with a final transition edge in a mapping simplex
statement:
Use small simplicial sets, standard simplices and weak homotopy equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and coherent realization $\mathfrak C$ and simplicial mapping sets of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison]. Let $n>0$ and let $A_0\leftarrow\cdots\leftarrow A_n$ be any chain of small simplicial sets. Define $M$ by $M_r=\coprod_{\alpha:[r]\to[n]}(A_{\alpha(r)})_r$, with operators $(\alpha,a)\mapsto(\alpha\theta,t_{\alpha(r),\alpha\theta(s)}\theta^*a)$ for $\theta:[s]\to[r]$, where $t_{j,i}:A_j\to A_i$ is the chain composite. For a vertex $y\in A_n$, put $y'=t_{n,n-1}(y)$ in the fiber over $n-1$, and let $e:y'\to y$ be the edge of $M$ represented by $n-1\leq n$ and $s_0y\in(A_n)_1$. For every vertex $x$ of $M$ over an index less than $n$, enriched composition with the vertex $[e]\in\mathfrak C[M](y',y)_0$ is a weak homotopy equivalence
$$\mathfrak C[M](x,y')\xrightarrow{[e]\circ-}\mathfrak C[M](x,y).$$
No quasicategory or fibration hypothesis on any $A_i$ or on $M$ is imposed.

source.place: HTT Lemma 3.2.2.9, printed pp. 182–183 Read online 2026-10-17; WANTED: archive under literature/. No Stacks tag states this simplicial result.

proof.text: Factor $t_{n,n-1}:A_n\to A_{n-1}$ in the Joyal model structure as a monomorphism $i:A_n\hookrightarrow B$ followed by a trivial fibration $p:B\twoheadrightarrow A_{n-1}$. Replace only $A_{n-1}$ by $B$, take $i$ as the last transition, and, if $n>1$, take $t_{n-1,n-2}p:B\to A_{n-2}$ as the preceding transition. This gives a commutative ladder to the original chain, with $p$ in position $n-1$ and identities elsewhere. The termwise-equivalence node gives a Dwyer--Kan equivalence $\mathfrak C[M(\widetilde A)]\to\mathfrak C[M(A)]$. If $x$ is over $n-1$, choose a lift $\widetilde x\in B_0$ using the lifting square $\varnothing\hookrightarrow\Delta^0$ against $p$; otherwise use the unchanged vertex. The final vertex $y$ is unchanged; its penultimate image is $i(y)$, which maps to $y'=p(i(y))$, and the degenerate simplex $s_0y$ defines a final edge $\widetilde e$ mapping exactly to $e$. Naturality of enriched composition gives a commutative square for composition with these edges, with both vertical maps weak homotopy equivalences. Two-out-of-three reduces the desired claim to the new chain. Thus assume that the last transition is a monomorphism. No lift of an earlier transition is necessary: its replacement is the displayed composite.

Put $T=\Delta^{\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}$, $I=\Delta^{\{n-1,n\}}$, $K=T\amalg_{\{n-1\}}I$, $M_-=M(A_0\leftarrow\cdots\leftarrow A_{n-1})$, and $D=\mathfrak C[M_-]$. The inclusion $K\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ is inner anodyne already in the weak-saturation convention: attach every pair of missing faces $\sigma$ and $\sigma\cup\{n-1\}$, where $n\in\sigma$, $n-1\notin\sigma$, and $\sigma$ contains an earlier vertex, in increasing order of $|\sigma|$. Each attachment is an inner horn missing the face opposite $n-1$: deleting $n$ leaves a face of $T$, and deleting any earlier vertex leaves a previously attached face or a face of $I$. Every missing simplex occurs in exactly one such pair. For $n=1$ the inclusion is the identity. Since a left lifting class is closed under pushouts and finite composites, it also has the left lifting property against every inner fibration. Apply the inner-anodyne pushout-product node with $\varnothing\hookrightarrow A_n$ to obtain an inner anodyne monomorphism $u:A_n\times K\hookrightarrow A_n\times\Delta^n$. To pass from the lifting convention of the pushout-product node to the weak-saturation convention of the coherent-inner-anodyne node, apply [lem-coef-small-object-cell-factorization] to the small set of inner horns and $\kappa=\aleph_0$. Simplicial colimits are degreewise, and each horn has finitely many nondegenerate simplices: a map into an increasing union factors through one finite stage, and equality of two such maps is detected at a later stage. This checks the required smallness. The factorization node identifies the left lifting class with arrow retracts of inner-horn cell maps, which belong to the weakly saturated class. Thus $u$ has the weak-saturation meaning as well. Its realization is Dwyer--Kan by the coherent-inner-anodyne node and a Bergner cofibration by the left Quillen functor $\mathfrak C$, hence a trivial cofibration.
The defining simplex formula gives $M=M_-\amalg_{A_n\times T}(A_n\times\Delta^n)$: a simplex whose last base vertex is $n$ occurs uniquely in the second part, and a simplex whose last vertex is less than $n$ is identified with its transitioned image in $M_-$. Since $\mathfrak C$ is a left adjoint, it preserves this pushout. Set $C_0=D\amalg_{\mathfrak C[A_n\times T]}\mathfrak C[A_n\times K]$ and $C=\mathfrak C[M]$. Then $C=C_0\amalg_{\mathfrak C[A_n\times K]}\mathfrak C[A_n\times\Delta^n]$. Thus $j:C_0\to C$ is a pushout of the trivial cofibration $\mathfrak C[u]$ and is itself a trivial cofibration. Indeed a lifting problem against any fibration pulls back to one for $\mathfrak C[u]$, and its filler descends through the pushout. This argument needs no cofibration hypothesis on $\mathfrak C[A_n\times T]\to D$.

source.place: Lemma 3.2.2.9, first two pushout diagrams, pp. 182–183; expanded inner-horn filtration argument.

proof.text:
Write $E=\mathfrak C[A_n]$ and $H=\mathfrak C[A_n\times I]$. The pushout decomposition of $K$ and preservation of colimits simplify the preceding expression to $C_0=D\amalg_E H$, with $E\to D$ induced by $A_n\hookrightarrow A_{n-1}\hookrightarrow M_-$ and $E\to H$ the initial endpoint. The first simplicial map is degreewise injective by the standing last-transition monomorphism and the explicit fiber inclusion in $M_-$, so its realization $E\to D$ is a Bergner cofibration. Therefore $H\to C_0$ is a cofibration: its lifting problems pull back to those for $E\to D$, and pushout universality descends the fillers. By the product clause of the existing homotopy-exponentials node, the comparison $q:H\to E\times\mathfrak C[I]$ is a Dwyer--Kan equivalence. Form
$$C_0'=C_0\amalg_H(E\times\mathfrak C[I]).$$
Bergner left properness applied to $q$ and the cofibration $H\to C_0$ proves that $F:C_0\to C_0'$ is Dwyer--Kan. Here $H$ is the realization of the full final interval $A_n\times\Delta^{\{n-1,n\}}$, including its edges; it is not the realization of a two-point discrete set.

source.place: Lemma 3.2.2.9, final product pushout, p. 183; Corollary 2.2.5.6, p. 93.

proof.text: The subset-poset formula gives $\mathfrak C[I]=[1]$ with discrete mapping sets. Thus $C_0'=D\amalg_E(E\times[1])$, gluing the initial copy of $E$ by $f:E\to D$. It has an old part $D$ and a final copy of $E$, with no arrows back to the old part. In simplicial degree $r$, a mixed arrow from $x\in D$ to the final copy of $b\in E$ is represented by $(v,u)$ with $v\in D(x,f(a))_r$, $u\in E(a,b)_r$, modulo $(f(h)v,u)\sim(v,uh)$ for $h\in E(a,a')_r$, $v\in D(x,f(a))_r$ and $u\in E(a',b)_r$. This is the degreewise word description of the pushout: a word crosses from the old part to the final part exactly once, and all initial-copy arrows can be absorbed in $D$. The map $[v,u]\mapsto f(u)v$ to $D(x,f(b))_r$ has inverse $w\mapsto[w,1_b]$; the displayed relation makes both composites identities. These maps commute with every simplicial operator. The old-old mapping sets remain those of $D$. With $b=y$ and $f(b)=y'$, postcomposition with the interval edge is precisely $w\mapsto[w,1_y]$, and hence is an isomorphism $C_0'(Fx,Fy')\to C_0'(Fx,Fy)$.

source.place: Lemma 3.2.2.9, final observation, p. 183; explicit pushout universal-property/co-Yoneda calculation.

proof.text: Let $e_0$ be the final edge in $C_0$. The two functors $j:C_0\to C$ and $F:C_0\to C_0'$ carry $e_0$ respectively to $[e]$ and the interval edge, and preserve composition strictly. For $F$ this gives a commutative square whose top row is $e_0\circ-:C_0(x,y')\to C_0(x,y)$, bottom row is the isomorphism in Step 4, and both vertical maps are weak homotopy equivalences by the definition of Dwyer--Kan equivalence. Two-out-of-three makes the top row weak. The analogous square for $j$ has the same top row, the desired composition map in $C=\mathfrak C[M]$ as bottom row, and both vertical maps weak. Two-out-of-three now gives the claim. In particular there is no map $C_0'\to C$ being assumed. Step 1 transports the result to the original chain with exactly its chosen vertices and edge. All constructions allowed arbitrary small simplicial sets and used no fibrancy hypothesis.
